source: SPEC §7 (TreatyFeed, OptionTerms) with CR #5-#7; units: premium_change_pct and lr_adjustment_pts in percent points
treatymodel_note: Compared on 25 Oct 2026 with treatymodel 2.0 (PBM treatymodel/spec.py and build.py, branch claude/inspiring-rubin-7ncppi). The treaty tool has no file import: scenario inputs are typed or pasted into its Scenarios library. Gaps G1-G4 below are open (CR #23); treatymodel_verified stays false until the owner decides them.

inputs.scenario_general: prem_chg 'Premium change % (all books)' and lr_chg 'Loss ratio change (+/- pts, all books)': fractions (cell format +0.0%, 0.02 = +2 pts)
inputs.per_book: volume 'Volume factor (x experience premium)' fraction, default 1.0; lr_adj 'LR adjustment (+/- pts)' fraction; er_ovr; ff_rate
inputs.per_reinsurer: RI_TERMS: basis (Net/Gross premium), comm_type (None/Flat/Sliding), comm_flat, comm_max, comm_lr_max, comm_min, comm_lr_min, fee_rate, fee_base, corr_from, corr_to, cap, ps_type (Tiered/Margin share/None), ps_exp, ms_share, tiers t1-t4 (u, s, f), lr_basis, ps_base, lr_override; all percentages as fractions
inputs.share_matrix: share of each book per reinsurer (fraction, total per book <= 100%)

gaps.G1_units: TreatyFeed premium_change_pct and lr_adjustment_pts are in percent (CR #7); the tool takes fractions: divide by 100 on entry
gaps.G2_premium_change_level: TreatyFeed gives a premium change per treaty book; the tool has one premium change per scenario (all books) and a per-book volume factor. Per-book entry would be volume = 1 + premium_change_pct / 100 (rate factor x (1 - lapse)): owner to confirm
gaps.G3_terms_structure: OptionTerms carries the Terms sheet as free text; the tool needs structured terms (commission type and rates, corridor from / to, cap, profit share type and tiers) and a share per book. Numeric commission / profit share / corridor / cap / share exist only in terms_scores.csv (scorecard input)
gaps.G4_book_names: treaty_book values (treaty_book_map.csv) must equal the tool's Setup book names; at most 8 books, 6 reinsurers (options) and 12 scenarios per workbook
